name: Odd vs even unison: center mono vs ultra-wide
goal: Choose odd vs even unison voice counts deliberately: odd counts keep a centered, in-tune voice for mono-compatible leads/basses/pads front-and-center in the mix; even counts leave a center gap for ultra-wide L/R leads—then set detune and blend to taste.

source.title: Odd vs Even Unison in Serum | The Secret to Wide & Focused Sounds

prerequisites: Synth with multi-voice unison, detune, and stereo spread/blend (or Web Audio multi-osc detune pan)

inputs.name: voice_count
inputs.description: Unison voices (try 2–8+; compare odd vs even)

outputs.name: unison_voicing_choice
outputs.description: Odd or even unison setup with detune/blend notes

constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there.

Original synthesis / signal-flow only — map brand UI (Serum/Vital/Ableton/etc.) to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Prefer transferable parameter relationships over vendor-specific preset or bank names.
Portable idea: odd voice counts place one voice dead-center; even counts spread L/R with a center gap—independent of Serum UI.

steps.action: Start from 1 voice, then set 2 voices: expect one left and one right with a center gap; default detune often sounds harsh—lower detune.
steps.expect: Hard L/R split, weak mono center

steps.action: Switch to 3 (odd) voices: confirm a center voice appears; with blend lowered you hear more of that center while keeping similar detune.

Compare 4 (even) vs 5 (odd) at similar detune: higher even counts can sound more detuned/wide; very high odd counts (e.g. ~15) pack many voices near center so the patch can sound *less* detuned than a mid even count.
For reese/detuned saw bass or other front-and-present mix parts, prefer odd voice counts for mono compatibility (center represented).
steps.expect: Bass/lead holds center in mono check

steps.action: For an uber-wide lead you will pan off-center, even counts (2/4/…) with blend favoring outer voices are acceptable.
Example starting detune for chord/lead work: modest (~0.16 in the video’s demo); reset blend to default then adjust; always A/B odd vs even in context.

verification: Odd count shows/audibly centers one voice; even count has center gap
Front-of-mix bass/pad uses odd; intentionally wide side lead may use even
Mono fold keeps center energy on odd-count patches
